subject: Music Production
title: Binaural Hearing and Spatial Sense
description: A quick win: understand Binaural Hearing and Spatial Sense.

hook.text: You can tell where a sound comes from without looking because you have two ears, not one.

buildup.text: Sound reaches your closer ear a tiny fraction of a second before it reaches the far ear.

discovery.text: Your brain measures this time difference and calculates the direction the sound came from.

twist.text: Headphone producers exploit this by adding micro-delays to simulate three-dimensional sound.

climax.text: Spatial audio in modern production uses binaural tricks to place sounds all around the listener.

punchline.text: A tiny time gap between ears creates 3D sound.

quiz.question: How does the brain determine where a sound comes from?
options: By the volume difference between ears
By the time difference of arrival between both ears
By the pitch of the sound
